metadata.name: DOH Policy on the Abu Dhabi Health Information Exchange (ADHIE)
metadata.description: The Department of Health (DOH) Abu Dhabi Policy on the Abu Dhabi Health Information Exchange (ADHIE) establishes the regulatory framework for the meaningful exchange of health information between Health System Stakeholders across the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. It defines roles, responsibilities, and strategies for universal stakeholder and patient participation, data management (system access, enterprise security, data use, breaches), data quality (interoperability, integrity), and implementation arrangements (escalation, enforcement, monitoring) — including detailed procedural roles applicable to DOH, Healthcare Facilities, and the ADHIE Operator.
metadata.source_organization: Department of Health (DOH), Abu Dhabi - Strategy Division
metadata.classification_reasoning: This is a regulatory policy issued by DOH Abu Dhabi (Document Ref: DOH/POL/STR/HIE/1.1/2020) that applies to the entire healthcare sector of Abu Dhabi. It is a mandatory policy framework defining obligations for DOH, Healthcare Facilities, and the ADHIE Operator. Non-compliance carries escalation/enforcement consequences including license suspension/withdrawal and financial penalties.
metadata.framework_purpose: To articulate the Emirate's vision and goal for the ADHIE by setting out DOH's sector-wide objectives and strategies to ensure that all Health System Stakeholders can actively participate in and benefit from the meaningful and safe exchange of health information.
metadata.framework_scope: The entire healthcare sector of Abu Dhabi — all DOH-licensed Healthcare Facilities, Healthcare Professionals, Authorized Users, the ADHIE Operator, and DOH itself, as participants in or operators of the Abu Dhabi Health Information Exchange (ADHIE) Platform.
framework_objectives: Universal stakeholder participation by all Healthcare Facilities as Data Suppliers to the ADHIE Platform
Universal patient participation by maximizing the number of patients whose data is available through ADHIE
Safe access, storage, transmission, and proper use of healthcare data through clear System Access, Enterprise Security, Data Use, and Breach management
Interoperability and high-quality data through open-standards based interfaces and data quality controls
Engagement of Health System Stakeholders with clear roles and responsibilities
Escalation and enforcement of policy compliance with defined sanctions
Continuous monitoring and evaluation of ADHIE performance
metadata.target_audience: DOH-licensed Healthcare Facilities, Healthcare Professionals, Authorized Users, ADHIE Operator, CIOs, CISOs, IT Steering Committees, Privacy & Compliance Officers, Internal Audit teams of all healthcare entities in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi
required_artifacts: Participant Agreement signed with ADHIE Operator
Authorized User agreements and consent statements
Breach response policy and incident records
metadata.penalty_for_non_compliance: DOH escalation and enforcement may include: advice, remedial action plan, reprimand/notice/warning, suspension notice, withdrawal of licensure, recommendation of legal proceedings, fines and penalties pursuant to Applicable Laws, and reimbursement rate adjustments. ADHIE Operator may immediately suspend or terminate a Participant's right to Transact Patient Data and access the ADHIE Platform.
adoption_approach: Healthcare Facility enters Participant Agreement with ADHIE Operator
Complete readiness assessment and develop a compliant Participant System per ADHIE Platform Interface Standards
Adhere to the ADHIE Launch Schedule for onboarding
Implement internal policies (Access Control, Awareness/Training, Breach Response, Data Quality, Interoperability) aligned with Participation Criteria
Train and certify all Authorized Users prior to access; perform annual refresher training
Operationalize Patient consent process; share legacy data per DOH mandate where consent is unavailable
Maintain ADHICS compliance for all systems and processes using ADHIE data
Submit Patient Data and receive incoming Data per Participation Criteria SLAs
Report breaches to ADHIE and DOH within 5 working days; notify affected patients within 60 days

controls.description: All Healthcare Facilities shall seek patient consent for the sharing of Patient Data via the ADHIE in accordance with all DOH's Policies, including by incorporating the following into their standard...
controls.full_text: All Healthcare Facilities shall seek patient consent for the sharing of Patient Data via the ADHIE in accordance with all DOH's Policies, including by incorporating the following into their standard patient consent forms from the effective date of this policy: (4.2.2.2.1) Patients consent to the sharing of their Patient Data via the ADHIE whether it is newly-generated or past Patient Data. controls.title: ADHIE — System Interoperability Standards (Content and Transport)
controls.description: ADHIE shall establish system interoperability standards that may include the following: (4.
controls.full_text: ADHIE shall establish system interoperability standards that may include the following: (4.4.2.2.1) Domain Data Content and Structure Standards: includes information models, data naming standards, and controlled vocabularies. These represent semantic specifications that support business process level Interoperability. (4.4.2.2.2) Messaging and Transport Standards: covering message packaging, transport and network protocols. These may be considered more in the realm of syntactic standards that support technical interoperability. Examples include: (4.4.2.2.2.1) Private Network: Use of a private network service should be considered as part of a risk analysis, that transports all messaging through a private Wide Area Network (WAN). (4.4.2.2.2.2) SSL: Alternatively, secure data transport over the public Internet may utilize Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) protocol, the most widely adopted security protocol standard for the Internet. (4.4.2.2.2.3) 'Web services' are the industry standard for platform neutral, distributed application Interoperation over the Internet. Web services should be used to effect data sharing across the ADHIE Platform.

controls.description: ADHIE shall have the right to immediately suspend or terminate a Participant's right to Transact Patient Data, interface with the ADHIE Platform and access or use the ADHIE Platform if entitled to do...
controls.full_text: ADHIE shall have the right to immediately suspend or terminate a Participant's right to Transact Patient Data, interface with the ADHIE Platform and access or use the ADHIE Platform if entitled to do so under the Participant Agreement and/or if any one or more of the following occurs: (5.2.2.1.1) the Participant breaches or no longer satisfies the Participation Criteria for any reason; (5.2.2.1.2) the Participant no longer is a holder of any licence, consent, permit, authorisation, clearance or other approval necessary to enable the Healthcare Facility to operate as a Healthcare Facility in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi or no longer has any medical malpractice insurance or other insurance Policies required by Applicable Law; (5.2.2.1.3) the Participant commits a material breach of any of its obligations under this Policy or the Participant Agreement which is incapable of remedy, or which is capable of remedy but fails to remedy it or persists in such breach after 30 days of having been required in writing to remedy or desist; (5.2.2.1.4) the Participant is not in compliance with any Applicable Laws or if the ADHIE Operator is aware or reasonably believes any development may have a material impact on the Participant's ability to perform its obligations under this Participant Agreement effectively and in accordance with Applicable Laws; (5.2.2.1.5) the Participant is subject to an Insolvency event. Each Participant shall notify the ADHIE Operator if it experiences any Insolvency Event; (5.2.2.1.6) the relevant Participant breaches, or the ADHIE Operator reasonably suspects the relevant Participant is in breach of this Policy or any related Applicable Laws; (5.2.2.1.7) ADHIE Operator is instructed to suspend or terminate the Participant's right to Transact Patient Data, interface with the ADHIE Platform and access or use the ADHIE Platform by the DOH; and/or (5.2.2.1.8) the relevant Participant undergoes a Change of Control not previously approved in writing by the ADHIE Operator. Each Participant shall notify the ADHIE Operator if it experiences any Change of Control.
